newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Other" Franco-German talks tackle hard farm issues.
newsitem.headline: "Other" Franco-German talks tackle hard farm issues.

text.p: French and German farm ministers met in Paris on Friday and found broad agreement on most issues ahead of key European Union farm negotiations later this month, the French agriculture ministry said.

It was the first such meeting since France's new Socialist-led government took office last week, and -- like the far more visible Franco-German summit taking place 200 miles (260 km) away in Poitiers -- appeared to focus on issues which have seen Paris and Bonn pulling in opposite directions recently.
The two sides have been at loggerheads for months about whether to do away with the EU's controversial land-idling programme known as set-aside, which Bonn wants strengthened.

France's new Socialist farm minister Louis Le Pensec has not said whether he will carry through pledges by his centre-right predecessor Philippe Vasseur to try to axe the system, which is deeply unpopular with French farmers.
"The discussions focused mainly on negotiations for the annual farm package which is on the agenda for European Union farm ministers in Luxembourg on June 23," a statement said.
"This meeting showed broad convergence of views between the ministers on most aspects of this negotiation," it said, but did not say whether this included agreement on set-aside.
A Franco-German compromise is seen as crucial for a set-aside agreement which would affect autumn grain sowings for next year's harvest and have some impact on world food prices.

Analysts say German Farm Minister Jochen Borchert, one of the most experienced of the current batch of EU farm leaders, would prefer to raise the proportion of land left fallow from the current five percent to help maintain high producer prices.

EU grain industry sources said last week there was however an increasing likelihood that set-aside, seen as the most sensitive part of the EU's annual farm package, should be left where it is because grain stocks would again be low this summer.

Le Pensec and Borchert met on the same day German Chancellor Helmut Kohl flew to western France for talks on Europe with French President Jacques Chirac and the country's new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
